Figure 1:Initialization matters.Top row:each method’s initialization;bottom row:the corresponding refined output. The highlighted box marks a large unobserved region. (a) LiDiff[19]starts from Gaussian noise that carries
no information about the scene; (b) LiNeXt[6]perturbs the input with a fixed noise variance, so its points stay near the observed surface and never reach across the gap; (c) Our adaptive module learns data-dependent displacements that populate the region from the surrounding geometry, and this coverage is preserved in both the coarse initialization and the final refined result.

Figure 2:Overview of RapidLiDAR.TheMulti-Scale Feature Extractionmodule (center) voxelizes the input point cloudX∈ℝM×3X\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times 3}and extracts multi-scale 3D voxel features(F1,F2,…,Fn)(F_{1},F_{2},\dots,F_{n})and a dense 2D BEV feature mapBdenseB_{\text{dense}}. TheAdaptive Initialization Module(top) predicts a spatially varying displacementΔ\Deltafor each point inP~\tilde{P}to obtain the initialized scenePinitP_{\text{init}}. TheMulti-Scale Reconstruction Module(bottom) projects voxel features into BEV feature maps and cross-attends per-point features fromPinitP_{\text{init}}with the multi-scale BEV feature maps using multi-scale deformable attention. A final MLP predicts a residual displacement that aligns each point with the underlying target surfaces, producing the completed scene.
Figure 4:Qualitative Comparison on SemanticKITTI.Our method produces more complete geometry in large occluded regions compared to prior methods.
